course_catalog.title: Introduction to Computer Science 1
course_catalog.description: Introduction to programming and computational problem solving in Python. Covers variables, control flow, functions, recursion, lists and dictionaries, basic object-oriented programming and simple algorithm analysis.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Write and debug small Python programs; decompose problems into functions; use recursion and basic data structures; reason informally about running time.

course_catalog.title: Introduction to Computer Science 2
course_catalog.description: Second course in programming using Java. Object-oriented design, abstract data types, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, hash tables and heaps, with an introduction to asymptotic analysis of algorithms.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Implement core data structures in Java; choose a data structure for a task; analyse algorithms with big-O notation; apply OOP principles.

course_catalog.title: Combinatoric Structures
course_catalog.description: Mathematical foundations of computer science: logic, sets, functions, relations, proof techniques including induction, counting and combinatorics, graphs and discrete probability.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Write proofs by induction and contradiction; solve counting problems; reason about graphs and relations; apply discrete probability.

course_catalog.title: Computer Systems
course_catalog.description: How computers execute programs: data representation, C and assembly language, memory hierarchy and caches, linking, processes, and an introduction to operating system concepts.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Program in C and read assembly; explain number representation; reason about memory and caching; describe process and OS abstractions.

course_catalog.title: Introduction to the Analysis of Algorithms
course_catalog.description: Design and analysis of algorithms: greedy methods, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, graph algorithms, network flow, and NP-completeness.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Design algorithms with standard paradigms; prove correctness; analyse running time; recognise NP-complete problems.

course_catalog.title: Geometric Algorithms
course_catalog.description: Linear algebra through a computational lens: vectors, matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalues, least squares, and applications to graphics, data and machine learning.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Solve linear systems; compute eigen-decompositions; apply linear algebra to geometric and data problems in code.

course_catalog.title: Algebraic Algorithms
course_catalog.description: Algebraic structures used in computing: modular arithmetic, groups, rings and fields, with applications to cryptography and error-correcting codes.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Apply number theory and abstract algebra to RSA, hashing and coding; implement algebraic algorithms.

course_catalog.title: Probability in Computing
course_catalog.description: Probability for computer scientists: discrete and continuous random variables, expectation, variance, concentration bounds, Markov chains, and randomized algorithms.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Model computing problems probabilistically; compute expectations and tail bounds; analyse randomized algorithms.

course_catalog.title: Concepts of Programming Languages
course_catalog.description: Programming language concepts: syntax, semantics, type systems, functional programming, interpreters, and comparison of language paradigms.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Implement an interpreter; reason about types and scope; program in a functional style.

course_catalog.title: Elements of the Theory of Computation
course_catalog.description: Theory of computation: finite automata, regular languages, context-free grammars, Turing machines, decidability and complexity classes.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Construct automata and grammars; prove languages non-regular; prove undecidability; reason about P and NP.

course_catalog.title: Fundamentals of Computing Systems
course_catalog.description: Fundamentals of computing systems: performance modelling, queueing, concurrency, synchronization, scheduling and resource management in operating systems.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Model system performance; write concurrent programs; analyse scheduling and synchronization.

course_catalog.title: Introductory Microeconomic Analysis
course_catalog.description: Introductory microeconomics: supply and demand, consumer and producer behaviour, market structures, market failure and the role of government.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Use supply-and-demand models; analyse firm behaviour across market structures; evaluate policy interventions.

course_catalog.title: Introductory Macroeconomic Analysis
course_catalog.description: Introductory macroeconomics: GDP, unemployment, inflation, economic growth, money and banking, and monetary and fiscal policy.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Interpret macroeconomic indicators; use AD-AS models; explain monetary and fiscal policy effects.

course_catalog.title: Intermediate Microeconomic Analysis
course_catalog.description: Intermediate microeconomic theory using calculus: consumer choice, production and cost, general equilibrium, game theory and welfare.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Solve constrained optimisation problems; derive demand and supply; analyse strategic interaction.

course_catalog.title: Intermediate Macroeconomic Analysis
course_catalog.description: Intermediate macroeconomic theory: long-run growth models, business cycles, IS-LM and AD-AS frameworks, open-economy macroeconomics and policy.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Build and solve growth and business-cycle models; evaluate stabilisation policy.

course_catalog.title: Empirical Economics 1
course_catalog.description: Empirical economics 1: probability, sampling distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing and simple regression with economic data.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Conduct hypothesis tests; estimate and interpret simple regressions; use statistical software.

course_catalog.title: Empirical Economics 2
course_catalog.description: Empirical economics 2: multiple regression, causal inference, instrumental variables, panel data and differences-in-differences, with an applied research project.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Estimate multivariate models; identify causal effects; complete an empirical project.

course_catalog.title: General Psychology
course_catalog.description: Survey of psychology: research methods, biological bases of behaviour, perception, learning, memory, development, personality, social behaviour and psychological disorders.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Describe major areas of psychology; explain basic research methods; apply concepts to everyday behaviour.

course_catalog.title: Experimental Design in Psychology
course_catalog.description: Experimental design in psychology: formulating hypotheses, designing experiments, controlling variables, ethics, data collection and analysis, and writing APA-style lab reports. Includes a lab component.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Design and run an experiment; analyse data with t-tests and ANOVA; write an APA-style research report.

course_catalog.title: Physiological Psychology
course_catalog.description: Physiological psychology: neurons, neurotransmission, brain anatomy, sensory and motor systems, sleep, motivation, emotion, learning and memory from a biological perspective.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain neural signalling; relate brain systems to behaviour; evaluate biological research methods.

course_catalog.title: Perception and Behavior
course_catalog.description: Perception and behaviour: sensory transduction, visual and auditory perception, psychophysics, attention and perceptual organisation.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain perceptual processes; apply psychophysical methods; relate perception to behaviour.

course_catalog.title: Introduction to Cognitive Psychology
course_catalog.description: Introduction to cognitive psychology: attention, memory, language, problem solving, reasoning and decision making.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain models of memory and attention; evaluate cognitive experiments; apply theories to real-world cognition.

course_catalog.title: Developmental Psychology
course_catalog.description: Developmental psychology across the lifespan: physical, cognitive, social and emotional development from infancy through adulthood.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Describe developmental stages and theories; evaluate developmental research designs.

course_catalog.title: Psychology of Personality: Theories and Application
course_catalog.description: Psychology of personality: trait, psychodynamic, humanistic and social-cognitive theories; personality assessment and applications.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Compare personality theories; evaluate assessment methods; apply theory to case material.

course_catalog.title: Social Psychology
course_catalog.description: Social psychology: attitudes, persuasion, conformity, group processes, prejudice, attraction and prosocial behaviour.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain core social-psychological phenomena; evaluate classic and modern studies.

course_catalog.title: Psychopathology
course_catalog.description: Psychopathology: classification, causes and treatment of psychological disorders including anxiety, mood, psychotic and personality disorders.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Describe DSM classification; explain aetiology models; compare treatment approaches.

course_catalog.title: Biology 1
course_catalog.description: Biology 1: chemistry of life, cell structure and function, metabolism, cell division, Mendelian and molecular genetics. Includes laboratory.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain cell structure and metabolism; solve genetics problems; perform basic lab techniques.

course_catalog.title: Biology 2
course_catalog.description: Biology 2: evolution, biodiversity, plant and animal physiology, and ecology. Includes laboratory.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain evolutionary mechanisms; describe organismal physiology; analyse ecological data.

course_catalog.title: Cell Biology
course_catalog.description: Cell biology: membranes, organelles, protein trafficking, cytoskeleton, cell signalling and the cell cycle.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain cellular processes at molecular level; interpret experimental cell-biology data.

course_catalog.title: Genetics
course_catalog.description: Genetics: Mendelian inheritance, linkage and mapping, chromosome biology, gene regulation, mutation and population genetics.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Solve transmission and mapping problems; explain gene regulation; apply population-genetics models.

course_catalog.title: General Chemistry 1
course_catalog.description: General chemistry 1: atomic structure, stoichiometry, chemical bonding, gases, thermochemistry and periodic trends. Includes laboratory.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Perform stoichiometric calculations; explain bonding and periodic trends; carry out lab measurements.

course_catalog.title: General Chemistry 2
course_catalog.description: General chemistry 2: kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, thermodynamics and electrochemistry. Includes laboratory.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Solve equilibrium and kinetics problems; apply thermodynamics; analyse electrochemical cells.

course_catalog.title: Organic Chemistry 1
course_catalog.description: Organic chemistry 1: structure, bonding, stereochemistry, nomenclature, substitution and elimination reactions. Includes laboratory.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Name organic compounds; predict reaction mechanisms; perform organic lab techniques.

course_catalog.title: Organic Chemistry 2
course_catalog.description: Organic chemistry 2: aromatic compounds, carbonyl chemistry, spectroscopy and multistep synthesis. Includes laboratory.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Interpret NMR and IR spectra; plan multistep syntheses.

course_catalog.title: Calculus I
course_catalog.description: Calculus I: limits, continuity, derivatives and their applications, and an introduction to integrals.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Compute limits and derivatives; solve optimisation and related-rates problems; evaluate basic integrals.

course_catalog.title: Calculus II
course_catalog.description: Calculus II: techniques of integration, applications of integration, sequences, series and Taylor series.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Apply integration techniques; test series for convergence; build Taylor approximations.

course_catalog.title: Multivariate Calculus
course_catalog.description: Multivariate calculus: vectors, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector calculus including Green's and Stokes' theorems.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Compute partial derivatives and multiple integrals; apply vector calculus theorems.

course_catalog.title: Linear Algebra
course_catalog.description: Linear algebra: systems of equations, matrices, vector spaces, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and orthogonality.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Solve linear systems; work with vector spaces; compute eigenvalues; prove basic results.

course_catalog.title: Differential Equations
course_catalog.description: Differential equations: first-order equations, linear second-order equations, systems of equations, Laplace transforms and qualitative analysis.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Solve ODEs analytically; analyse systems qualitatively; model physical systems.

course_catalog.title: Discrete Mathematics
course_catalog.description: Discrete mathematics: logic, proofs, sets, relations, functions, combinatorics, recurrence relations and graph theory.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Construct proofs; solve combinatorial and recurrence problems; reason about graphs.

course_catalog.title: Probability
course_catalog.description: Probability theory: axioms, random variables, joint distributions, expectation, limit theorems and an introduction to stochastic processes.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Compute probabilities and expectations; apply the law of large numbers and CLT.

course_catalog.title: Introduction to Program Design and Implementation
course_catalog.description: Introductory program design using Python with a required lab. Data-driven design, functions, conditionals, lists, iteration, recursion and testing.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Design programs systematically from data definitions; write tested functions; use recursion and lists.

course_catalog.title: Program Design and Implementation 1
course_catalog.description: Program design and implementation 1 with lab: object-oriented design in Java, classes, interfaces, inheritance, testing and abstraction. Data structures are covered mainly in CS 2700.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Design class hierarchies; write unit tests; apply abstraction and encapsulation in Java.

course_catalog.title: Program Design and Implementation 2
course_catalog.description: Program design and implementation 2 with lab: larger-scale software design, design patterns, modularity, and team projects.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Apply design patterns; build multi-module applications; collaborate using version control.

course_catalog.title: Discrete Structures
course_catalog.description: Discrete structures: logic, sets, proof by induction, counting, probability, graphs, and modular arithmetic for computer science.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Write inductive proofs; solve counting and probability problems; reason about graphs.

course_catalog.title: Data Structures and Analysis
course_catalog.description: Data structures and analysis with lab: lists, stacks, queues, trees, heaps, hash tables, graphs and asymptotic analysis.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Implement and analyse standard data structures; select structures for performance.

course_catalog.title: Algorithms and Data
course_catalog.description: Algorithms and data: divide and conquer, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, graph algorithms and intractability.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Design and analyse algorithms; prove correctness; identify NP-hard problems.

course_catalog.title: Computer Systems
course_catalog.description: Computer systems: C programming, machine representation, assembly, memory management, processes, threads and file systems.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Program in C; explain memory and process abstractions; write basic concurrent code.

course_catalog.title: Theory of Computation
course_catalog.description: Theory of computation: automata, regular and context-free languages, Turing machines, computability and complexity.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Build automata; prove undecidability; reason about complexity classes.

course_catalog.title: Programming Languages
course_catalog.description: Programming languages: semantics, interpreters, type systems and language design.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Implement interpreters; reason about type safety and semantics.

course_catalog.title: Logic and Computation
course_catalog.description: Logic and computation: propositional and predicate logic, formal reasoning about programs, and theorem proving.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Prove program properties formally; use a theorem prover.

course_catalog.title: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
course_catalog.description: Mathematical foundations of AI: linear algebra, probability and optimisation applied to machine-learning models.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Apply linear algebra and probability to ML; implement gradient-based optimisation.

course_catalog.title: Principles of Microeconomics
course_catalog.description: Principles of microeconomics: markets, supply and demand, elasticity, firm behaviour, competition and market failure.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Analyse markets with supply and demand; compare market structures; assess policy.

course_catalog.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
course_catalog.description: Principles of macroeconomics: national income, unemployment, inflation, growth, money and stabilisation policy.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Interpret macro data; use AD-AS models; explain monetary and fiscal policy.

course_catalog.title: Microeconomic Theory
course_catalog.description: Microeconomic theory with calculus: consumer and producer theory, equilibrium, game theory and welfare.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Solve optimisation problems; analyse equilibrium and strategic behaviour.

course_catalog.title: Macroeconomic Theory
course_catalog.description: Macroeconomic theory: growth, business cycles, IS-LM, open economy and policy analysis.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Build macro models; evaluate policy using formal frameworks.

course_catalog.title: Statistics for Economists
course_catalog.description: Statistics for economists: probability, estimation, hypothesis testing and simple regression using economic data.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Run hypothesis tests; estimate simple regressions; interpret results.

course_catalog.title: Applied Econometrics
course_catalog.description: Applied econometrics: multiple regression, specification, heteroskedasticity, and an applied data project. Limited coverage of instrumental variables.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Estimate and diagnose regression models; complete an applied project.

course_catalog.title: Foundations of Psychology
course_catalog.description: Foundations of psychology: methods, neuroscience, sensation, learning, memory, development, social behaviour and disorders.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Describe major psychological domains; explain research methods.

course_catalog.title: Statistics in Psychological Research
course_catalog.description: Statistics in psychological research: descriptive statistics, probability, t-tests, ANOVA, correlation and regression using software. Little coverage of designing or running experiments.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Compute and interpret descriptive and inferential statistics; report results in APA style.

course_catalog.title: Biological Psychology
course_catalog.description: Biological psychology: neurons, neurotransmitters, brain systems, sensation, motivation, emotion and memory.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain neural mechanisms of behaviour; evaluate biological research.

course_catalog.title: Social Psychology
course_catalog.description: Social psychology: attitudes, social influence, group behaviour, prejudice and relationships.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain social-psychological phenomena; evaluate research.

course_catalog.title: Developmental Psychology
course_catalog.description: Developmental psychology from infancy through adolescence and adulthood.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Describe developmental theories and stages; evaluate research designs.

course_catalog.title: Psychology of Language
course_catalog.description: Psychology of language: speech perception, word recognition, sentence processing and language acquisition.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain models of language processing and acquisition.

course_catalog.title: Foundations of Biology
course_catalog.description: Foundations of biology with lab: biomolecules, cells, metabolism, genetics and evolution.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain cellular and genetic principles; perform lab techniques.

course_catalog.description: Genetics and molecular biology with lab: inheritance, DNA replication, transcription, translation, gene regulation and molecular techniques.

course_catalog.title: Biochemistry
course_catalog.description: Biochemistry with lab: protein structure, enzymes, metabolism and bioenergetics.

course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Describe major areas of psychology.

course_catalog.title: Research Methods in the Behavioral Sciences
course_catalog.description: Research methods in the behavioural sciences: hypotheses, experimental and correlational designs, ethics, data collection, descriptive and basic inferential statistics, and an APA-style research proposal. Includes a small lab experiment.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Design a simple experiment; apply research ethics; analyse data with t-tests; write an APA report.

course_catalog.title: General Biology I
course_catalog.description: General biology I with lab: chemistry of life, cells, metabolism, cell division and genetics.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain cell structure and genetics; perform lab techniques.

course_catalog.title: General Chemistry I with Lab
course_catalog.description: General chemistry I with lab: atomic structure, stoichiometry, bonding, gases and thermochemistry.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Perform stoichiometric calculations; explain bonding.

course_catalog.title: English Composition I
course_catalog.description: English composition I: academic writing, argument, research and citation.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Write a researched argumentative essay.

course_catalog.title: Fitness and Wellness
course_catalog.description: Fitness and wellness: personal fitness planning, nutrition and healthy lifestyle.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Design a personal fitness plan.

course_catalog.title: Linear Algebra
course_catalog.description: Linear algebra (10-week quarter): systems of linear equations, matrices, determinants, vector spaces, eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Solve linear systems; compute eigenvalues; work with vector spaces.

course_catalog.title: Calculus for Science I
course_catalog.description: Calculus for science I (quarter): limits, derivatives and applications.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Compute derivatives; solve applied problems.

course_catalog.title: Calculus for Science II
course_catalog.description: Calculus for science II (quarter): integrals, techniques and applications of integration.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Evaluate integrals; apply integration.

course_catalog.title: Programming Abstractions in Python
course_catalog.description: Programming abstractions in Python (quarter): recursion, object-oriented programming, linked structures, trees and basic algorithm analysis.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Write recursive and object-oriented Python; implement linked structures.

course_catalog.title: Algorithms and Abstract Data Types
course_catalog.description: Algorithms and abstract data types (quarter): sorting, graph algorithms, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms and asymptotic analysis.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Design and analyse algorithms.

course_catalog.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
course_catalog.description: Intermediate microeconomics (quarter): consumer and producer theory with calculus, market equilibrium.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Solve optimisation problems; derive demand.

course_catalog.title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
course_catalog.description: Intermediate macroeconomics (quarter): growth, business cycles and policy models.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Build macro models.

course_catalog.title: Introduction to Econometrics
course_catalog.description: Introduction to econometrics (quarter): regression, inference and applied data analysis.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Estimate and interpret regressions.

course_catalog.title: Behavioral Economics
course_catalog.description: Behavioral economics (quarter): heuristics, biases, time preference, social preferences and field experiments.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Explain behavioural deviations from rational choice.

course_catalog.title: Introduction to Psychology
course_catalog.description: Introduction to psychology (quarter): survey of psychological science.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Describe major areas of psychology.

course_catalog.title: Research Methods in Psychology
course_catalog.description: Research methods in psychology (quarter) with lab: experimental design, measurement, ethics, ANOVA and APA writing.
course_catalog.learning_outcomes: Design and run an experiment; write an APA report.

syllabi.title: Data Structures in Java
syllabi.syllabus: Week 1-2 Java review, classes and interfaces. Week 3-4 Linked lists and iterators. Week 5 Stacks and queues. Week 6 Recursion. Week 7 Midterm. Week 8-9 Binary search trees. Week 10 Hash tables. Week 11 Heaps and priority queues. Week 12-13 Sorting (insertion, merge, quick) and searching. Week 14 Big-O analysis. Week 15 Final project. Assessment: 6 programming assignments 40%, midterm 25%, final 35%. Contact hours: 3 lecture + 2 lab per week. Textbook: Data Structures and Abstractions with Java.

syllabi.title: Research Methods in the Behavioral Sciences
syllabi.syllabus: Week 1 Science and psychology. Week 2 Ethics and IRB. Week 3 Measurement, reliability and validity. Week 4 Survey and correlational designs. Week 5-6 Experimental designs, control and confounds. Week 7 Midterm. Week 8 Descriptive statistics. Week 9 t-tests. Week 10 Intro to ANOVA (one-way only). Week 11-13 Class lab experiment: design, data collection, analysis. Week 14 APA-style writing. Week 15 Final paper. Assessment: lab report 35%, exams 40%, homework 25%. Contact hours: 3 lecture + 1 lab per week.

syllabi.title: Linear Algebra
syllabi.syllabus: 10-week quarter. Wk 1 Linear systems and row reduction. Wk 2 Matrix algebra. Wk 3 Inverses and LU. Wk 4 Determinants. Wk 5 Midterm; vector spaces. Wk 6 Subspaces, basis, dimension. Wk 7 Linear transformations. Wk 8 Eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Wk 9 Diagonalisation, orthogonality. Wk 10 Least squares, review. Assessment: weekly homework 20%, midterm 30%, final 50%. Contact: 4 lecture hours/week.

syllabi.title: Program Design and Implementation 1
syllabi.syllabus: OOP in Java: classes, interfaces, inheritance, polymorphism, generics, unit testing, abstraction, simple design patterns. Lab weekly. Data structures (trees, hashing, heaps) are deferred to CS 2700.

syllabi.title: Statistics for the Behavioral Sciences
syllabi.syllabus: Descriptive statistics, probability, sampling distributions, z and t tests, one- and two-way ANOVA, correlation and regression, nonparametric tests. Problem sets in R. No lab and no research project.

syllabi.title: Introduction to Econometrics
syllabi.syllabus: Wk 1-2 Review of probability and statistics. Wk 3-5 Simple and multiple OLS regression. Wk 6 Midterm. Wk 7 Heteroskedasticity and specification. Wk 8 Binary dependent variables. Wk 9 Instrumental variables (introduction). Wk 10 Applied project presentations. Software: Stata.
